item.title: I announced my divorce on Instagram and then AI impersonated me
item.description:
📝 Enough people have received the memo about divorce etiquette to ask whether a person’s divorce is a “congratulations” or “sorry” situation. In the app, all the original text from my post was pulled in along with some additional text following my sign-off line of WATCH THIS SPACE that I certainly didn’t author. From finding support from friends to prioritizing what matters most, I explore the themes of identity, worth, and finding happiness after divorce.
🔗 Read more: https://eiratansey.com/2025/12/20/i-announced-my-divorce-on-instagram-and-then-ai-impersonated-me/

item.title: More on whether useful quantum computing is “imminent”
item.description:
📝 More on whether useful quantum computing is “imminent” These days, the most common question I get goes something like this: A decade ago, you told people that scalable quantum computing wasn’t imminent. After returning from Q2B, I then did an hour-long podcast with “The Quantum Bull” on the topic “How Close Are We to Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing. To be sure, the detailed list of quantum speedups expands over time (as new quantum algorithms get discovered) and also contracts over time (as some of the quantum algorithms get dequantized).
🔗 Read more: https://scottaaronson.blog/?p=9425

item.title: The gift card accountability sink
item.description:
📝 [0]Gift card scams are also enormous. Most businesses do not run their own gift card programsThere exists an ecosystem of gift card program managers, who are essentially financial services businesses with a sideline in software. There is also a large regulatory component to running a gift card program, despite gift cards’ relatively lax regulatory drag (we’ll return to that in a moment).
